title: DOOM (shareware)
subtitle: id Software, 1993 · episode one from id's own 1.9 shareware archive, served as published and unpacked in the page; linuxdoom-1.10, the only source ever published
argsHint: empty starts the game as it shipped: title screen, attract demos, and a key opens the menu. `-warp <episode> <map> -skill <1-5>` drops straight into a level; `-playdemo <name>` replays one. **`-grabmouse` is what turns the mouse on** -- id left `PointerMotionMask` commented out in i_video.c:802, so the window never asks X for motion; the XGrabPointer behind -grabmouse is what does.

needsData.hint: doom19s.zip as id published it (idgames, idstuff/doom/): DEICE.EXE and DOOMS_19.1, .2, joined and unpacked in the page

_soundServer: Doom delegates sound to a separate PROCESS -- doomdef.h defines SNDSERV and i_sound.c popens './sndserver' -- so making it audible was never an audio problem. Naming the source here is enough: web/worker.js starts a second worker on it and connects the two with a byte pipe.
_mouse: Two conditions, both id's own. -grabmouse selects the motion events (i_video.c:847). And i_video.c:257 posts the event only `if (x != X_width/2 && y != X_height/2)` -- an AND, so a purely HORIZONTAL movement is discarded by the game itself. Doom needs both axes to move before it turns.
_archive: The shareware archive allows passing on the archive, not its files (README.TXT, DOOMS_19.DAT: PLEASE DISTRIBUTE!!!), so the archive is what the data root holds and the page unpacks it (web/unpack.js, needsData.archive).
